title: Secrets leakage: the key spreads through tool arguments into the transcript and log
summary: Disclosure of the billing API credential to anyone who can read the log or the tool-call record.

LC.rationale: The exposure is created by an ordinary user task with no attacker-supplied natural language; the model simply passes the key from its prompt as the api_key argument, so no natural-language control path to security-relevant behaviour is present.

CP.rationale: The secret is written into the run transcript and tool-call record, which is stored source content re-read by a log reader, not attacker-controlled context that alters agent memory or standing behaviour.

AP.rationale: The lab is a single agent with no handoffs, and the disclosure is confined to the transcript and tool-call record of the initially affected component.

RH.rationale: The transcript log is a monitor artifact the agent can write, but no evaluator, verifier or reward channel is on the path and no reward-hacking episode is observed or tested.

ES.rationale: The baseline offers all twelve built-in tools with unvalidated arguments, and remote MCP tool descriptions and schemas are fetched every run and trusted unpinned, so the extension binding surface is unvetted.

agentic_applicability.rationale: The lab models the agent as a tool-using office assistant that chooses and sequences tool calls, and the S6 exploit test uses a scripted worst-case model that does what the vulnerable prompt tells it.
